detail:
The CDC describes rheumatoid arthritis (RA) as an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, mainly the lining of the joints. That inflammation can cause pain, swelling, and stiffness, often in the hands, wrists, and knees on both sides of the body, and RA can also affect other parts of the body such as the eyes, lungs, and heart.

Symptoms can include aching or stiffness in more than one joint, tenderness and swelling, weight loss, fever, and fatigue, and they often develop gradually. The CDC notes that clinicians diagnose RA through a physical exam, lab tests, X-rays, and a review of health history, usually with a rheumatologist involved. Because joint damage can begin early, sources emphasize diagnosing and starting treatment as soon as possible after symptoms begin.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about evaluation for rheumatoid arthritis symptoms.
sourceName: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summary: The CDC gives an overview of rheumatoid arthritis, how it affects the joints and body, how clinicians diagnose it, and why early diagnosis and treatment matter.
takeaways: rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease that inflames the joints
symptoms can include joint pain, swelling, stiffness, and fatigue
diagnosis combines an exam, lab tests, x-rays, and health history
early treatment helps limit joint damage
title: Rheumatoid arthritis: immune inflammation in the joints
